changelog.entry: Four new practice boards, two before the first valve and two before the first mixer. Life Support now opens with two small boards that each have a single valve, and The Core opens with two small boards that each have a single mixer, so you can learn the new part before the big boards. The valves and mixers themselves have not moved. The station is now 44 rooms, and the map and the repair log have the four new rooms. Your saved rooms are untouched.

Every deck and room is now open from the start. You no longer patch five rooms to open the next deck: pick any room on the map or in the list, in any order. The deck order and the station map stay as they were, so new parts still arrive deck by deck, but nothing is locked. Your saved rooms are untouched.

Optional soft sounds, off unless you turn them on in Settings (Sound): a quiet tone when a line is joined, a low click when one is cut or taken back, and a bell when a room is fully restored. They are made in your browser (no sound files), stay silent in a hidden tab, and have a volume and a Reduce sounds switch. Nothing in the game depends on them.

A Desktop layout for wide windows: the board fills the stage, the tally sits in a side column, and the Station map, Repair log, Achievements and Settings open as windows from icons or the Menu (Esc). It is the same game and the same save; the Classic layout is unchanged and is still what phones use.

Fourteen achievements, none timed or luck-based, each with a visible count, in a new Achievements panel with a share button. Patching and restoring rooms, crossing lines on a bridge, going through a valve, using a mixer, taking a line back and climbing the hint ladder all count.

An opening screen (New Game, Continue, Saves), a short skippable tutorial, an About page that says what the game will never do, a keyboard shortcut list (press ?), a light theme, and a story toggle that hides the repair-log lines if you only want the puzzles. Nothing about the boards changed.

The whole station: forty rooms in five decks. The Crew Deck has holes where the hull is gone, Engineering adds bridges, Life Support adds one-way valves, and The Core adds mixers where two lines meet. Patched rooms light up on a station map and add a line to the repair log, and a free hint ladder (a nudge, a hint, then the answer) is there on every board.

Hull Repair opens: join matching ports on a damaged space-station board with lines that never cross. The first deck, the Docking Ring, has eight boards. Joining every line patches a room; covering every cell as well restores it. Drag from a port, drag back to shorten a line, tap its end to take a cell back. Nothing is timed.
